The face labels in the upper row from left to right are F, G, H, 5; the face labels in the lower row from left to right are J, 9, 3, K. The figure also draws a small schematic diagram of an octahedron, explaining that this net folds into a regular octahedron. Reasoning: When folded according to the net, the four upper-row triangles F, G, H, 5 will meet at one vertex; the four lower-row triangles J, 9, 3, K will meet at the opposite vertex. The boundary points between adjacent rhombuses correspond to vertices on the equator, and each such vertex is composed of two adjacent upper faces and two lower faces. Let the common sum at each vertex be M, then there are: Upper vertex: F+G+H+5=M. Lower vertex: J+9+3+K=M. Equator vertices include: F+J+G+9=M, G+9+H+3=M, H+3+5+K=M, 5+K+F+J=M. Comparing the upper vertex F+G+H+5 with the equator vertex G+9+H+3 gives F+G+H+5=G+H+12, so F=7. Comparing the upper vertex F+G+H+5 with F+J+G+9 gives H+5=J+9, so H=J+4. Comparing the upper vertex F+G+H+5 with H+3+5+K gives F+G=K+3. Substituting F=7 gives G+7=K+3, so K=G+4. Among the numbers 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, F is already 7, so G, H, J, K use 2, 4, 6, 8. From H=J+4, (J,H) can only be (2,6) or (4,8). From K=G+4, (G,K) can only be (2,6) or (4,8). The two groups must not repeat each other, so if J=2, then G=4; if J=4, then G=2. In either case, G+J=6.

method.method_draft: First read the net in the image as four connected diamond-shaped pairs of triangular faces in a row: top labels, from left to right, are F, G, H, 5, and bottom labels are J, 9, 3, K. When folded into the octahedron, the four top triangles meet at one apex, the four bottom triangles meet at the opposite apex, and each boundary point between adjacent diamonds becomes an equatorial vertex where the two neighboring top faces and two neighboring bottom faces meet. Write the equal vertex-sum equations: top apex F+G+H+5, bottom apex J+9+3+K, and equatorial vertices such as F+J+G+9, G+9+H+3, H+3+5+K, and 5+K+F+J. Compare the top apex equation with the middle equatorial equation G+9+H+3 to get F=7. Then compare adjacent equatorial/top equations to get H=J+4 and K=G+4. Since F uses 7, the remaining letters G,H,J,K are 2,4,6,8. The relations force one pair to be (J,H)=(2,6) or (4,8), and the other pair to be (G,K)=(4,8) or (2,6), so in either case G+J=6.

Image description: The octahedron net in the attached figure is composed of four connected rhombuses, and each rhombus is divided by a horizontal line into an upper and a lower triangle. The face labels in the upper row from left to right are F, G, H, 5; the face labels in the lower row from left to right are J, 9, 3, K. The figure also draws a small schematic diagram of an octahedron, explaining that this net folds into a regular octahedron.

Reasoning: When folded according to the net, the four upper-row triangles F, G, H, 5 will meet at one vertex; the four lower-row triangles J, 9, 3, K will meet at the opposite vertex. The boundary points between adjacent rhombuses correspond to vertices on the equator, and each such vertex is composed of two adjacent upper faces and two lower faces.
Let the common sum at each vertex be M, then there are:
Upper vertex: F+G+H+5=M.
Lower vertex: J+9+3+K=M.
Equator vertices include: F+J+G+9=M, G+9+H+3=M, H+3+5+K=M, 5+K+F+J=M.
Comparing the upper vertex F+G+H+5 with the equator vertex G+9+H+3 gives F+G+H+5=G+H+12, so F=7.
Comparing the upper vertex F+G+H+5 with F+J+G+9 gives H+5=J+9, so H=J+4.
Comparing the upper vertex F+G+H+5 with H+3+5+K gives F+G=K+3. Substituting F=7 gives G+7=K+3, so K=G+4.
Among the numbers 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, F is already 7, so G, H, J, K use 2, 4, 6, 8. From H=J+4, (J,H) can only be (2,6) or (4,8). From K=G+4, (G,K) can only be (2,6) or (4,8). The two groups must not repeat each other, so if J=2, then G=4; if J=4, then G=2. In either case, G+J=6.
